literal: Many subjects even though having learned, benefit they indeed do not have, in a good assembly, well so as to be received, those who do not speak.
translation: Even though they have learned many subjects, those who cannot speak in a way that penetrates the minds of a good assembly are of no use at all.
modern: நல்ல சபையிலே கேட்பவர் மனதில் பதியும்படி நன்றாக எடுத்துச் சொல்லத் தெரியாதவர்கள், பல நூல்களைக் கற்றிருந்தாலும் அதனால் ஒரு பயனும் இல்லாதவர்களே ஆவர்.
explanation: This couplet emphasizes that the ultimate test of learning is the ability to communicate it effectively to others. The word 'பல்லவை' refers to many diverse subjects of study, and 'செல' means to penetrate or go deep into the minds of the listeners. Those who fail to speak clearly and convincingly before a good assembly ('நல்லவையுள்') render all their extensive education useless ('பயமிலரே'). True knowledge must be accompanied by the courage and skill to articulate it, otherwise, it remains locked away and serves no purpose.
